14.0.0 (2023-11-26)
===================
ripgrep 14 is a new major version release of ripgrep that has some new
features, performance improvements and a lot of bug fixes.

The headlining feature in this release is hyperlink support. In this release,
they are an opt-in feature but may change to an opt-out feature in the future.
To enable them, try passing `--hyperlink-format default`. If you use [VS Code],
then try passing `--hyperlink-format vscode`. Please [report your experience
with hyperlinks][report-hyperlinks], positive or negative.

[VS Code]: https://code.visualstudio.com/
[report-hyperlinks]: https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/discussions/2611

Another headlining development in this release is that it contains a rewrite
of its regex engine. You generally shouldn't notice any changes, except for
some searches may get faster. You can read more about the [regex engine rewrite
on my blog][regex-internals]. Please [report your performance improvements or
regressions that you notice][report-perf].

[report-perf]: https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/discussions/2652

Finally, ripgrep switched the library it uses for argument parsing. Users
should not notice a difference in most cases (error messages have changed
somewhat), but flag overrides should generally be more consistent. For example,
things like `--no-ignore --ignore-vcs` work as one would expect (disables all
filtering related to ignore rules except for rules found in version control
systems such as `git`).

[regex-internals]: https://blog.burntsushi.net/regex-internals/

**BREAKING CHANGES**:

* `rg -C1 -A2` used to be equivalent to `rg -A2`, but now it is equivalent to
  `rg -B1 -A2`. That is, `-A` and `-B` no longer completely override `-C`.
  Instead, they only partially override `-C`.

Build process changes:

* ripgrep's shell completions and man page are now created by running ripgrep
with a new `--generate` flag. For example, `rg --generate man` will write a
man page in `roff` format on stdout. The release archives have not changed.
* The optional build dependency on `asciidoc` or `asciidoctor` has been
dropped. Previously, it was used to produce ripgrep's man page. ripgrep now
owns this process itself by writing `roff` directly.

Performance improvements:

* [PERF #1746](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/issues/1746):
  Make some cases with inner literals faster.
* [PERF #1760](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/issues/1760):

# Burntsushi-Ripgrep Engineering Brief Answers

## 1. Bug where using the same matching style for several patterns could skip one

When multiple glob patterns used the same matching strategy (e.g., multiple literal patterns, or multiple suffix patterns), ripgrep's `matches_all` check only verified that the strategy itself matched, not that all globs within that strategy matched. This could cause patterns to be incorrectly skipped. The fix added a `matches_all` method to each strategy to properly count all pattern matches within that strategy.

**Commit:** f55548b globset: fix `matches_all` false positives
**Quote:** "Make sure that we correctly check that all globs are matched, even if multiple globs use the same strategy."

## 2. Bug where curly-brace file filters stopped finding anything inside those bundled folders

[NOT FOUND - Despite extensive searching through the git history, I could not locate a specific bug report or commit that matches this description. The most related work I found was 5f5da48 which added support for nested alternates in curly braces, but that was a feature request, not a bug fix. There was also f34fd5c which added support for empty alternates in patterns like `foo{,.txt}`, but that also appears to be a feature rather than a bug fix.]

## 3. Slowdown on Windows from checking whether every single ignore file exists

On Windows, ripgrep was introduced to an additional `stat` call for every single directory entry to determine if it was a directory. This was disastrous for performance. The fix leveraged the fact that on Windows, metadata is available for free when reading directories, avoiding the extra system call.

**Commit:** d65966e ignore: fix performance regression on Windows
**Quote:** "we introduced an additional stat call for every single directory entry, which can be quite disastrous for performance."

## 4. Everyone just wanted paths given relative to the directory the command was set up for

The `--sortr=path` flag (reverse sort by path) was left unimplemented with a `todo!()` call that made it into a release. When implemented, it sorts files in reverse alphabetical order relative to the search root directory.

**Commit:** daa157b core: actually implement --sortr=path
**Quote:** "This is an embarrassing oversight. A `todo!()` actually made its way into a release!"

## 5. Bug that only started showing up after we moved past that earlier release

In ripgrep 14.1.1, a bug was discovered in the inner literal extraction logic that could produce false negatives. When multiple optimization strategies collided, the regex `(?i:e.x|ex)` would not match `e-x` when it should have. The issue was in how literal sequences were unioned - the `prefix` attribute wasn't being correctly propagated, causing incorrect cross-products of extracted literals.

**Commit:** 9d738ad regex: fix inner literal extraction that resulted in false negatives
**Quote:** "the extracted literals in this case, after the fix, are `X` and `x`. They were considered 'exact' (i.e., lead to a match), but of course they are not. Observing an `X` or an `x` does not mean there is a match."

## 6. Search time hardly changed no matter how much trailing context you asked for

When using the `-A/--after-context` flag with large values, ripgrep was computing preceding lines based on `max_context()` (which includes before-context) rather than just `before_context`. When before-context was 0 but after-context was large (e.g., 999999), ripgrep would still scan back through the entire file looking for preceding lines, causing dramatic performance degradation. The fix limits the preceding line search to only what's needed for before-context.

**Commit:** d4b77a8 searcher: fix a performance bug with `-A/--after-context`
**Quote:** "we only need to find the N preceding lines based on before context. We can skip this (potentially costly, for large values of N) step when before_context==0."

# Burntsushi-Ripgrep Engineering Brief Answers

## 1. Bug where using the same matching style for several patterns could skip one

When multiple glob patterns used the same matching strategy (e.g., multiple literal patterns, or multiple suffix patterns), ripgrep's `matches_all` check only verified that the strategy itself matched, not that all globs within that strategy matched. This could cause patterns to be incorrectly skipped. The fix added a `matches_all` method to each strategy to properly count all pattern matches within that strategy.

**Commit:** f55548b globset: fix `matches_all` false positives
**Quote:** "Make sure that we correctly check that all globs are matched, even if multiple globs use the same strategy."

## 2. Bug where curly-brace file filters stopped finding anything inside those bundled folders

[NOT FOUND - Despite extensive searching through the git history, I could not locate a specific bug report or commit that matches this description. The most related work I found was 5f5da48 which added support for nested alternates in curly braces, but that was a feature request, not a bug fix. There was also f34fd5c which added support for empty alternates in patterns like `foo{,.txt}`, but that also appears to be a feature rather than a bug fix.]

## 3. Slowdown on Windows from checking whether every single ignore file exists

On Windows, ripgrep was introduced to an additional `stat` call for every single directory entry to determine if it was a directory. This was disastrous for performance. The fix leveraged the fact that on Windows, metadata is available for free when reading directories, avoiding the extra system call.

**Commit:** d65966e ignore: fix performance regression on Windows
**Quote:** "we introduced an additional stat call for every single directory entry, which can be quite disastrous for performance."

## 4. Everyone just wanted paths given relative to the directory the command was set up for

The `--sortr=path` flag (reverse sort by path) was left unimplemented with a `todo!()` call that made it into a release. When implemented, it sorts files in reverse alphabetical order relative to the search root directory.

**Commit:** daa157b core: actually implement --sortr=path
**Quote:** "This is an embarrassing oversight. A `todo!()` actually made its way into a release!"

## 5. Bug that only started showing up after we moved past that earlier release

In ripgrep 14.1.1, a bug was discovered in the inner literal extraction logic that could produce false negatives. When multiple optimization strategies collided, the regex `(?i:e.x|ex)` would not match `e-x` when it should have. The issue was in how literal sequences were unioned - the `prefix` attribute wasn't being correctly propagated, causing incorrect cross-products of extracted literals.

**Commit:** 9d738ad regex: fix inner literal extraction that resulted in false negatives
**Quote:** "the extracted literals in this case, after the fix, are `X` and `x`. They were considered 'exact' (i.e., lead to a match), but of course they are not. Observing an `X` or an `x` does not mean there is a match."

## 6. Search time hardly changed no matter how much trailing context you asked for

When using the `-A/--after-context` flag with large values, ripgrep was computing preceding lines based on `max_context()` (which includes before-context) rather than just `before_context`. When before-context was 0 but after-context was large (e.g., 999999), ripgrep would still scan back through the entire file looking for preceding lines, causing dramatic performance degradation. The fix limits the preceding line search to only what's needed for before-context.

**Commit:** d4b77a8 searcher: fix a performance bug with `-A/--after-context`
**Quote:** "we only need to find the N preceding lines based on before context. We can skip this (potentially costly, for large values of N) step when before_context==0."
